title: Deploy documentation from release tags and selected refs
description:
The release website remains at 0.9.0 because the documentation workflow only builds main, whose development version is published under `/dev/`.

Deploy documentation on `v*` tag pushes and allow manual deployment from a branch, tag, or commit. The workflow checks out the selected source before installing the package and building the site, so a release tag updates the stable site while main continues to update the development site.

Serialize deployments and publish `gh-pages` with a normal Git push, preserving its history and the existing development site.

Validation: `actionlint` and `git diff --check` pass. A full site build from the 0.10.0 release source updated the stable homepage to 0.10.0 and preserved all 180 development-site files byte for byte, along with the Git worktree metadata.

Refs #345.

title: Preserve public API compatibility and clarify breaking changes
description:
Preserve calls supported by torchvision 0.9.0 while keeping multi-image grids and S3 target classes. Positional calls such as `vision_make_grid(batch, FALSE, 4)` continue to treat the extra arguments as grid options, named `num_rows` controls the grid width, and detection and segmentation target transforms accept bare lists, including SAHI batches.

Internally, match scalar grid options against the released argument order, apply the width alias within the S3 methods, and reuse the existing target implementations for bare lists. Add public-API regression coverage.

Update NEWS, reference documentation and the classes vignette. Put breaking changes first, explain the existing Mask R-CNN `masks` / `mask_probs` migration, and distinguish saved-checkpoint incompatibilities from changes in forward behavior.

title: Fix bounding-box annotation alignment and remove partial recycling
description:
`draw_bounding_boxes()` now filters degenerate boxes together with their per-box labels and colors. Two boxes with two labels and one invalid box now draw the valid box with its original label instead of raising a broadcasting error.

**Breaking change:** supplied labels and colors must contain one shared value or one value per original box. Partial recycling now errors; `NULL` defaults remain supported.

Internally, box validation returns the selection mask, and annotation lengths are checked before filtering. Adds rendering and length-validation regressions, documents the contract in NEWS, and regenerates the reference with roxygen2 8.1.1.

title: Fix crop geometry and pixel-annotation alignment
description:
Fix crop geometry so annotations follow the pixels and every five- and ten-crop result has the requested size.

- Shift bounding boxes, including rotated boxes, with the padding applied during center crops.
- Sample integer random-crop origins over the complete valid range, including the last valid row and column.
- Correct the height, width, and corner arguments in five-crop, which also fixes ten-crop.

Internally, image and item center crops share one geometry calculation. Item center crops reuse the existing padding and cropping methods, removing duplicate box translation, clipping, filtering, and metadata code. Regression tests cover pixel–annotation alignment, padding on one or both axes, rectangular images, rotated boxes, transform composition, corner contents, and every five- and ten-crop output shape.

The MRE draws `item` before cropping, after cropping with main, and after cropping with this PR. White pixels are image content; the red rectangle is the annotation. Main leaves the box at `(10, 10, 20, 20)` while padding moves the white square to `(20, 20, 30, 30)`. This PR moves the box with the pixels. Images are enlarged fourfold for readability.

| `item` before                                                                                                                                                          | `item` after using main                                                                                                                                                        | `item` after using the PR branch                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ![item before cropping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlverse/torchvision/1c4fe5ed93345b78f0df7f1d31e9ac80838774b0/vignettes/examples/assets/crop-item-before.png) | ![item after center crop on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlverse/torchvision/1c4fe5ed93345b78f0df7f1d31e9ac80838774b0/vignettes/examples/assets/crop-item-main.png) | ![item after center crop on the PR branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlverse/torchvision/1c4fe5ed93345b78f0df7f1d31e9ac80838774b0/vignettes/examples/assets/crop-item-pr.png) |

Run from the PR checkout after creating a separate checkout of main:

```sh
git worktree add --detach /tmp/torchvision-crop-main-414 origin/main
```

```r
library(torch)
pkgload::load_all("/tmp/torchvision-crop-main-414", quiet = TRUE)

item <- list(x = torch_zeros(3, 100, 100), y = list())
item$x[, 11:20, 11:20] <- 1
item$y$boxes <- torch_tensor(rbind(c(10, 10, 20, 20)))

title: Fix RF-DETR numerical parity with roboflow/rf-detr
description:

- interpolate DINOv2 position embeddings with antialiased bicubic, as F.interpolate(antialias = TRUE) in the reference (run time and loader)
- official configs: small 3 decoder layers @512, medium 4 @576, base/base_2/base_o365 @560

title: fix: Faster R-CNN / Mask R-CNN inference parity with torchvision

title: Fix inception/resnet random init and honour the `progress` argument

- resnet: weight init and zero_init_residual looped over top-level children only; iterate over self$modules (recursive).
- download_and_cache() gains `progress = TRUE` and passes quiet = !progress to download.file(); every model constructor (except ViT/MaxViT, covered by #405) now forwards `progress`, including the Faster/Mask R-CNN backbones and MTCNN sub-networks.

title: Fix ConvNeXt UPerNet norms, detection defaults and drop_path
description:
- convnext_upernet_backbone now applies the per-stage LayerNorms norm0-3 of the official ConvNeXt segmentation backbone; the checkpoint's backbone.norm0-3 are mapped onto them and pretrained weights are loaded with strict = TRUE.
- model_convnext_*_upernet() default to num_classes = 150 when pretrained = TRUE.
- model_convnext_*_detection() default to num_classes = 90 and pass score_thresh, nms_thresh and detections_per_img to fasterrcnn_model(); the example uses coco_classes().
- ConvNeXt blocks implement stochastic depth in training mode; fix the model_convnext example and the parameter counts of the 22k models.

title: Fix MobileNetV3 / EfficientNet parity with torchvision
description:
- EfficientNet squeeze-and-excitation uses SiLU instead of ReLU (shared by v1 and v2).
- EfficientNetV2 uses BatchNorm eps = 1e-3; EfficientNet b5-b7 use eps = 1e-3, momentum = 0.01.
- MobileNetV3 uses BatchNorm eps = 1e-3, momentum = 0.01, gains a `norm_layer` argument and only calls $eval() when pretrained weights are loaded.
- Faster R-CNN MobileNetV3 backbones pass `norm_layer = nn_batch_norm2d` to keep torchvision's eps = 1e-5 detection backbone BN.
- Add stochastic depth to EfficientNet / EfficientNetV2 residual blocks (torchvision schedule).
- Passing `dropout` to effnet()/effnetv2() constructors no longer shifts positional arguments.
- mobilenet_v2 no longer builds blocks for a stage with n = 0.

title: Fix FCN dilation and DeepLabV3 aux_loss defaults
description:
- model_fcn_resnet50/101: use replace_stride_with_dilation = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE) (output stride 8) as in torchvision; outputs now match PyTorch exactly.
- model_fcn_resnet*: skip the ImageNet backbone download when pretrained = TRUE.
- model_fcn_resnet*: remove dead `strict =` / num_classes key-filtering code (torch's load_state_dict has no strict argument).
- model_deeplabv3_*: aux_loss = NULL now follows `pretrained`, as documented; document the actual pretrained_backbone default (FALSE).
- test-models-deeplabv3.R: argmax is 1-based, use factor levels 1:21.

title: Fix LW-DETR numerical parity with the reference implementation
description:
- C2f bottlenecks in the projector no longer add a residual (the reference builds them with shortcut = FALSE).
- The sine embedding of the query reference points used R's 1-based torch_arange(dim), shifting all frequencies; use 0..(dim - 1).
- model_lw_detr_large(): the P5 down-sampling ConvX uses ReLU (the reference ConvX default) instead of SiLU.
- Two-stage selection: zero memory and proposals at padded/invalid positions before enc_output, as in gen_encoder_output_proposals(), instead of masking after the norm and setting logits to -Inf.
- Docs: the reference evaluation stretches to 640x640; letterboxing with pixel_mask is an alternative, not the reference preprocessing.
- Add regression tests for the sine embedding and the bottleneck.

title: Fix facenet / MTCNN models to match facenet-pytorch
description:
- P/R/ONet: take the softmax over the class dimension (dim 2), not the batch.
- InceptionResnetV1: add the missing repeat_1 stage (5 x Block35, scale 0.17), rewrite Block35 (branch2 32->32->32, conv2d 96->256, residual then ReLU, no debug prints) and fix the swapped Mixed_6a branch1 paddings.
- InceptionResnetV1: pretrained = TRUE loads "vggface2", unknown values error, num_classes defaults to NULL so pretrained logits are kept.
- Tests, docs and NEWS updated.

title: Fix model_vit_*() ignoring the input and port model_maxvit() faithfully from PyTorch
description:
Description:

This PR fixes two pretrained vision transformers that currently do not classify images correctly.

## `model_vit_*()`: predictions do not depend on the input

`encoder_block` creates `nn_multihead_attention()` with the default `batch_first = FALSE`, but passes
`(batch, tokens, dim)` tensors. Attention therefore mixes the *same token position across the batch*
instead of the tokens of an image. Because the class token is identical for all images, the output
does not depend on the image at all:

```r
library(torch)
m <- torchvision::model_vit_b_32(); m$eval()
x1 <- torch_randn(1, 3, 224, 224); x2 <- torch_randn(1, 3, 224, 224)
with_no_grad(as.numeric((m(x1) - m(x2))$abs()$max()))
#> 0
```

In addition, the positional embedding was assigned to self$encoder$pos_embedding, where
self$encoder is a plain R list. It was therefore never registered as a parameter: it was neither
loaded from the pretrained weights, nor trained, nor moved to the device together with the model.

Changes:
- create the attention layers with batch_first = TRUE
- register the positional embedding as self$pos_embedding (and map encoder.pos_embedding to it when
  loading the weights)
- use eps = 1e-6 in the layer norms, as in the reference implementation

model_maxvit(): re-port from PyTorch's torchvision/models/maxvit.py

The previous implementation was a simplified approximation of MaxViT:
- window and grid attention were single-headed, and window attention attended over the whole feature map
  instead of 7x7 windows
- the relative position bias was never used (the index buffer was all zeros)
- the classifier was missing the tanh between its two linear layers
- the MBConv squeeze-excitation used GELU instead of SiLU, and the projection shortcut pooled after the
  1x1 convolution with a 2x2 average pool instead of a 3x3/stride-2 one before it
- the weights were loaded with strict = FALSE, which hid all of this

The new implementation follows the reference implementation module by module and keeps its parameter
names, so the existing weight file (maxvit.pth) is loaded with strict = TRUE. Inputs other than
224x224 are still supported, as long as the feature maps are divisible by the partition size (the
existing 448x448 test passes).

Verification

Both models now reproduce the reference implementation in PyTorch (torchvision 0.29) with identical
weights and inputs (two ImageNet-normalized photos and one random input):

┌──────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┐
│  model   │ max. absolute difference of the logits │ top-3 classes │
├──────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ vit_b_32 │ 6.9e-06                                │ identical     │
├──────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ maxvit   │ 5.0e-06                                │ identical     │
└──────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────┘

Before this PR, the pretrained ViT-B/32 predicted the same three ImageNet classes (stupa, knot, crane)
for every image, and the pretrained MaxViT did not predict a cat or dog class for any of six cat and dog
photos. With this PR, all six get cat or dog classes as their top-1 prediction.

Tests

- new regression tests for both models (no downloads needed): the output of an image depends on the
  image, but not on the other images in the batch, and for MaxViT all parameters (including the relative
  position bias tables) receive gradients
- a pretrained MaxViT test that checks that all weights are loaded and that the head can be replaced
  (num_classes = 10); runs with TEST_LARGE_MODELS=1
- test-models-vit.R and test-models-maxvit.R pass locally, including the large pretrained MaxViT tests

The output shapes of several transforms did not match what torchvision for python returns:

* `transform_crop()` clamped the crop to the image instead of padding it with zeros, so the output could be smaller than requested or empty.

While adding tests for the hue transformation two further bugs showed up:

* `hsv2rgb()` used `h * 6 - 1` instead of the fractional part of the sector and omitted the saturation in `t`, so converting to HSV and back did not return the original image.
* `transform_adjust_hue()` used `%%`, which is `fmod()` for tensors and keeps the sign of the dividend, so a negative `hue_factor` gave a black image. It now also rejects images that do not have 1 or 3 channels instead of silently dropping the additional ones.

title: fix: model_convnext_small_22k1k defaults to 1000 classes
description:
`convnext_small_22k1k` is pretrained on Imagenet 22k and *fine-tuned* on Imagenet 1k, so the published weights have a 1000-class head. The formal default was `num_classes = 21841`, taken from the other `_22k` models, so `model_convnext_small_22k1k(pretrained = TRUE)` built a 21841-class head and then failed to load the state dict with

  The size of tensor a (21841) must match the size of tensor b (1000)
  at non-singleton dimension 0

Verified against the published checkpoint: its `head.weight` is 1000x768, whereas `convnext_tiny_22k` really is 21841x768.

The caller could not work around this by passing `num_classes = 1000` either, because `.convnext()` loads the state dict with `strict = FALSE`, which is silently swallowed by `...`: `load_state_dict()` of torch for R has no `strict` argument.

The roxygen description had the two datasets the wrong way round ("pretrained on Imagenet 1k and fine-tuned on Imagenet 22k") and the variants table listed 21841 classes and a 252 MB file size; both are corrected (the file is 192 MB).

title: fix: honour aux_logits = FALSE for pretrained inception_v3
description:
`model_inception_v3()` forces `aux_logits = TRUE` when `pretrained = TRUE`, because the published state dict contains the `AuxLogits.*` tensors and would otherwise not load. The caller's original value was stored in `original_aux_logits`, but never used again, so `aux_logits = FALSE` was silently ignored for pretrained models.

As a consequence the network returned a `list(logits, aux_logits)` instead of a single tensor in training mode, which breaks generic training loops, and the parameters of the auxiliary branch were handed to the optimizer without ever receiving a gradient.

The auxiliary branch is now removed after the state dict has been loaded. Note that assigning `NULL` does not deregister a submodule in torch for R, hence `nn_identity()` is used, which brings the parameter count in line with a model that was constructed with `aux_logits = FALSE` from the start.

Closes #328

Implements LW-DETR ([https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03459](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03459)), a real-time detection transformer

Adds model_lw_detr_tiny(), model_lw_detr_small(), model_lw_detr_medium(), and model_lw_detr_large() with COCO-pretrained weights. The architecture comprises a ViT backbone, a C2f multi-scale projector, and a two-stage deformable-attention decoder. title: Add lw-detr models
description:
Closes #328

Adds four variants of the LW-DETR from the [Atten4Vis implementation](https://github.com/Atten4Vis/LW-DETR):

- model_lw_detr_tiny - ViT-Ti (6 layers, embed_dim=192), 100 queries
- model_lw_detr_small - ViT-Ti (10 layers, embed_dim=192), 300 queries
- model_lw_detr_medium - ViT-S (10 layers, embed_dim=384), 300 queries
- model_lw_detr_large - ViT-S (10 layers, embed_dim=384), 2-scale projector, 300 queries

The architecture is a ViT encoder with interleaved window or global attention, a C2f projector from the YOLOv8 and a 3-layer DETR decoder which has deformable cross-attention. Two-stage query selection and Group DETR which contains 13 groups are used during training but only the primary group is used at inference. The pretrained COCO weights are fetched via `download_and_cache()` . And all the four checkpoints load with zero missing or unexpected keys.

Since torchvisionlib #25 is still open, deformable cross-attention uses a pure PyTorch nnf_grid_sample fallback and no CUDA dependency. The CUDA operation can be swapped in once that issue is resolved.

The input images should be ImageNet-normalized tensors of shape (B, 3, H, W), square and divisible by 64.  640×640 would be  recommended . Output would be a list of detections per image with boxes i.e. xyxy pixels), labels, and scores.

title: Use torchvisionlib ops_nms when available for model_fasterrcnn and model_maskrcnn
description: Fixes #321 Fixes #322 **Changes:** - Dispatch nms() to torchvisionlib::ops_nms() when available in torchvisionlib. - Keep the pure R NMS implementation as the fallback. - Add coverage for fallback and native NMS dispatch. **What is the result of this pull-request on the actual end-to-end models it has an impact on ?** Before this PR, all six models, the four FasterRCNN variants and the two MaskRCNN variants, were running NMS entirely in pure R on every inference call. On a 520×520 image on CPU, that means that model_fasterrcnn_mobilenet_v3_large_320_fpn was taking around 25 seconds per image, with NMS being the main bottleneck. model_maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn was even worse taking around 1.7 minutes per image. After this PR, when torchvisionlib is installed, both models dispatch NMS to torchvisionlib::ops_nms() which is a native C++ implementation. The same FasterRCNN model now runs in about 2 seconds, and MaskRCNN drops to about 25 seconds. So FasterRCNN went from being unusably slow for interactive use to being reasonably fast and MaskRCNN went from taking nearly two minutes per image to under half a minute. For users who do not have torchvisionlib installed, nothing changes, the pure R fallback kicks in and behaviour is identical to before. This PR adds simple input validation to catch common mistakes when users pass invalid arguments to model functions.

### What changed
Added validation checks for `pretrained` and `progress` parameters in model functions. Now they properly check if you're passing TRUE/FALSE instead of accepting strings, numbers, or other invalid types.

### Why this matters
Users were getting confusing torch errors deep in the stack when they made simple mistakes like:
- `model_resnet18(pretrained = "yes")` instead of `TRUE`
- `model_vgg16(pretrained = 1)` instead of `TRUE`
- `model_alexnet(pretrained = c(TRUE, FALSE))` passing a vector

Now they get a clear message right away: `'pretrained' must be a single logical value`

### Implementation
- Added the same validation pattern to all model functions
- Uses the existing `value_error()` function that's already in the codebase
- Placed validation in helper functions where possible (so one check covers multiple models)
- Covers 50+ model functions: ResNet, VGG, AlexNet, MobileNet, EfficientNet, ViT, MaxViT, ConvNeXt, Inception, FCN, DeepLabV3, Faster R-CNN

## Summary
Split `coco_detection_dataset()` into two specialized datasets for object detection and instance segmentation tasks.

## Problem
- Current implementation carries 500MB+ annotation object in memory for entire dataset lifetime
- Confusing documentation mixing detection and segmentation use cases
- Tasks never run together (different model architectures)
- Poor cache organization with unidentified large files

**`coco_detection_dataset()`** - Object Detection Only
- Returns: boxes, labels, area, iscrowd
- Memory: ~250MB (50% reduction)
- Use: Faster R-CNN, YOLO, SSD

**`coco_segmentation_dataset()`** - Instance Segmentation (NEW)
- Returns: boxes, labels, area, iscrowd, segmentation, masks
- Memory: ~250MB
- Use: Mask R-CNN, DeepLab

**Cache Organization**: Files now stored in `/coco` subdirectory for better identification

## Breaking Change
Segmentation users must migrate:
```r
# Before

# After  
coco_segmentation_dataset(..., target_transform = target_transform_coco_masks)

title: remove zip::unzip
description:
This PR removes the dependency on `zip::unzip` added in version 0.4.0.

The problem is that `zip::unzip` may result in corrupted files. The following was seen on Fedora 37, unzipping the `tiny_imagenet` dataset:

- The line `unzip(raw_path, exdir = self$root_path)` creates a path `genet-200` (instead of unzipping to the given directory, which in this case is the same as the one the zip file is in)

- Some files are extracted correctly, but in `val/val_annotations.txt/`, there is nothing.
